hook: Your power bill went up. Blame a building you've never seen.
twist: On the biggest US grid (PJM, 67 million people), the yearly auction that pays power plants to stand ready went from $28.92 to $333.44 per megawatt-day in three auctions, and the grid's own market monitor puts most of the first jump on data centers.
angle: Why are electricity bills in the eastern US going up? Drawn as one page: the bill, the data center, the grid, the auction chart, the watchdog's estimate, the bill again.
why_now: The 2026/27 price ($329.17) took effect on 1 June 2026 and the record $333.44 for 2027/28 was set on 17 Dec 2025; power bills and data centers are in the news this autumn.
risks: Politically hot: explain the mechanism, no villains; SemiAnalysis argues the auction design, not AI itself, is the main cause, so the script attributes the 63% to the market monitor and says 'estimate'.
Bill impacts vary by utility zone: the only bill number shown is the D.C. Pepco example, labelled with who estimated it.
Forecasts of data-center demand may not come true (IEEFA); the script says 'forecasts', not 'demand'.
approved_by: user (2026-10-07: asked for a hand-drawn pilot telling 'stories happening around us'; topic picked by the builder under that brief)
